tasks.spec:
You are a test-tooling engineer. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge (detached at HEAD). Edit files here directly. NEVER git commit, never touch /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge itself, never run `uv`, never call a billed model or the network, never edit anything under storygame/, data/, bench/ or docs/, and never edit existing files under scripts/ or tests/. You own ONLY two NEW files: scripts/ringer/phase1/act2_guard_probe.py and tests/test_act2_guard_probe.py. First run: ln -s /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv .venv ; then use `PYTHONPATH=$PWD:$PWD/scripts/ringer/stage7 TMPDIR=/tmp .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_act2_guard_probe.py tests/test_act2_probe.py` and `.venv/bin/python -m ruff format <files>` / `-m ruff check <files>`.

CONTEXT. In the story package data/stories/continuity-initiative, the first turn of scene 2A is sometimes rejected by the narration guard (storygame/runtime/narration_safety.py, message "narration mentions unavailable knowledge 'cooling fault'"). The narrator is shown the phrase "cooling fault" three times in the SCENE section of its prompt, but "cooling fault" is also an auto-derived leak term: storygame/story_package/loader.py (_compile_knowledge_indexes, around lines 322 to 362) adds every multi-word must_convey phrasing of a knowledge entry to leak_term_to_knowledge when the entry sets no `leak_terms`, and knowledge entries k_sl_2a_c_r5 and k_sl_2a_c_r6 (data/stories/continuity-initiative/knowledge.yaml) have "cooling fault" in a must_convey group and no leak_terms. We want a bounded live sampling probe with three arms that replays the SAME first 2A turn many times. You build the probe and its free offline dry mode; a later, separately authorized step runs it live. Existing probe to imitate for structure and the billing guard: scripts/ringer/phase1/act2_probe.py (read it: `_state(package, scene_id)` builds the synthetic 2A arrival; `run`/`main` show the SpendBudget and counted_provider usage from scripts/ringer/stage7/door_transport.py, load_variation/provider_for from bench/core.py, RuntimeEngine from storygame/runtime/engine.py). An offline prompt-capture pattern that makes no network call is in scripts/ringer/stage7/payload_2b.py (mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {"CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL": "offline://..."}), then mock.patch.object CloudflareTurnProvider._request_item_facts and _request, raising a sentinel after capturing provider.last_prompt).

BUILD scripts/ringer/phase1/act2_guard_probe.py (import act2_probe the same way the existing probes import their siblings, with the same try/except ImportError style; importing helpers from it is fine, do not edit it):

1. ARMS = ("control", "wording", "leakterms"). `build_arm_package(arm, workdir: Path) -> Path` copies data/stories/continuity-initiative (shutil.copytree) to workdir/<arm>/ and applies EXACT string replacements, each of which must match exactly once or raise ValueError naming the arm and the missing text (never silently skip):
   - control: no edits.
   - wording, in knowledge.yaml: the line `  pressure: Prove the cooling fault is real to get inside` becomes `  pressure: Prove the cooling system is failing to get inside` (first search to confirm the exact text, whether it is quoted, and that it is unique; if the same phrase occurs in the line for another scene, scope the replacement to the 2A one and say so in a comment); the k_scene_2a_entry statement `Kristin and Brandon are at the facility gate and must prove the cooling fault is real to get inside.` becomes `Kristin and Brandon are at the facility gate and must prove the cooling system is failing to get inside.`; and in plot.md the scene 2A line `objective: Get inside by proving the cooling fault is real` becomes `objective: Get inside by proving the cooling system is failing`. Nothing else changes.
   - leakterms, in knowledge.yaml: insert one line directly after the `- id: k_sl_2a_c_r5` line and one directly after the `- id: k_sl_2a_c_r6` line (block-mapping key order is irrelevant), asserting first that the entry block has no existing leak_terms key. r5 line: `  leak_terms: [genuine cooling-water pressure fault, genuine pressure problem, genuine cooling fault, real ventilation fault, restricted infrastructure corridors, infrastructure corridors, restricted corridor access, console used]`. r6 line: `  leak_terms: [restricted infrastructure corridors, infrastructure corridors, restricted corridor access, console used]`. Nothing else changes.
   Every built package must load with storygame.story_package.loader.load_story_package(workdir/<arm>). If the loader rejects an edited copy, report that in the dry-run result and fail loudly; do not edit the loader or the repository data.
2. FIXED_COMMAND = "Inspect my work order beside the facility gate."  SCENE = "2A".  DEFAULT_N = 12.
3. Dry mode (`--dry-run`, makes NO network call and needs no .env): for the chosen arm, build and load its package, build the 2A state with act2_probe._state(package, "2A"), capture the exact narration prompt for FIXED_COMMAND offline (the payload_2b.py pattern; the capture must leave no request sent), and write <out>/results.json containing {"mode": "dry", "arm", "prompt_has_cooling_fault": bool, "leak_map_has_cooling_fault": bool, "leak_map_has_restricted_infrastructure_corridors": bool, "package": str(path)}. Find the leak map on the loaded package (package.knowledge_indexes.leak_term_to_knowledge; confirm the attribute and the key normalisation by looking at term_lookup_forms in the loader, and use that function to compute the keys you test). Expected, and asserted by the checker in dry mode: control has prompt True, map True; wording has prompt False, map True; leakterms has prompt True, map False, and its restricted_infrastructure_corridors key is True.
4. Live mode (no --dry-run) requires --confirm, else `raise SystemExit("live mode requires --confirm")`. For sample 1..n (--n, default 12, allowed 1 to 12): a fresh state from the arm's loaded package, `provider = provider_for(state, variation)` where variation = a COPY of load_variation(ROOT / "bench/variations/phase1-slice-current.json") with its `_package_path` set to the arm package path (verify nothing else reads the repository path), wrap with counted_provider under a SpendBudget with a hard Cloudflare cap of 60 requests for the whole arm run and NO player requests (confirm how the existing probe sets player_limit and make raw player calls impossible here; a test asserts the budget records no raw_player event). Run `RuntimeEngine(state, provider).turn(FIXED_COMMAND)` once. Record for each sample: {"sample": k, "result": "ok" | "rejected" | "transport_error", "error_class", "error_message", "error_code", "error_term" (getattr(e, "term", None), for ProposalValidationError), "narration" (segment texts joined by two newlines, only when ok), "recovery_count" and "request_count" read from the provider, "first_attempt_rejected": bool (true if the engine's last attempt carries a rejection even though the sample finished ok; mimic how act2_probe._run_row reads engine.last_attempt / engine.attempts)}. Classify ProposalValidationError (and any other guard rejection exception class used by the engine for a final rejection) as "rejected"; classify network or timeout exceptions (for example fetch failed, headers timeout, RuntimeError from the transport) as "transport_error" and carry on with the next sample; a SpendBudget cap error stops the run and is written to <out>/run-failure.txt (exit nonzero). Write <out>/results.json after EVERY sample (incremental) with {"mode": "live", "arm", "n", "command", "samples": [...], "caps": {"cloudflare": 60}, "budget_events": <the budget events list>}. After the loop write <out>/summary.json with counts per result and per error_term.
5. `--check <out> <n> [--dry]` (also exposed as a function `check(out: Path, n: int, mode: str) -> list[str]` returning error strings that start with "WHY "): in dry mode verify the expected booleans above for the recorded arm; in live mode verify exactly n samples, each with a valid result, narration non-empty for ok and absent otherwise, results counts consistent with summary.json, cloudflare events at most 60, zero raw_player events, and mode "live". Exit 0 only if no errors.
6. CLI: `--arm`, `--n`, `--out`, `--dry-run`, `--confirm`, `--check`. The arm package copy lives in a temporary directory under <out> (workdir=<out>/package) so artifacts are self-contained.

TESTS in tests/test_act2_guard_probe.py (new, keep it small and complete; do not touch existing tests): (a) for each arm, build_arm_package + load_story_package succeeds in tmp_path; (b) a dry run of each arm writes results.json and passes check(..., "dry"), asserting the expected-boolean table in item 3 of BUILD; (c) build_arm_package raises ValueError when a replacement target is missing (monkeypatch or patch a copied file in tmp_path so the text is absent); (d) live mode without --confirm raises SystemExit; (e) a live-mode test with a fake provider (monkeypatch provider_for to return a scripted provider that returns a valid narration payload, and a second that raises ProposalValidationError, and a third that raises a plain transport RuntimeError) checks the three result classes, that results.json is written incrementally, and that no raw_player budget event exists. No test may make a network call or need .env; unit tests must run hermetically. Player commands stay imperative first-person text.

OUTPUT. Leave changes uncommitted. Run ruff format on every Python file you create. The harness check runs your tests, a dry run of all three arms plus --check, ruff, confirms nothing else changed, and exports a patch.
tasks.check:
set -o pipefail
[ -e .venv ] || ln -s /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv .venv
export PYTHONPATH=$PWD:$PWD/scripts/ringer/stage7 TMPDIR=/tmp
PY=.venv/bin/python
git status --porcelain | grep -v '^?? .venv$' | awk '{print $2}' | sort > /tmp/g6chg.$$
printf '%s\n' scripts/ringer/phase1/act2_guard_probe.py tests/test_act2_guard_probe.py | sort > /tmp/g6alw.$$
[ -z "$(comm -23 /tmp/g6chg.$$ /tmp/g6alw.$$)" ] || { echo "WHY: files outside ownership changed:"; comm -23 /tmp/g6chg.$$ /tmp/g6alw.$$; exit 1; }
[ "$(wc -l < /tmp/g6chg.$$)" -eq 2 ] || { echo "WHY: both new files must exist"; cat /tmp/g6chg.$$; exit 1; }
$PY -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_act2_guard_probe.py tests/test_act2_probe.py > /tmp/g6pt.$$ 2>&1; RC=$?
tail -25 /tmp/g6pt.$$
[ $RC -eq 0 ] || { echo "WHY: tests failed"; exit 1; }
for A in control wording leakterms; do
  OUT=/tmp/g6-$A-$$; rm -rf $OUT
  $PY scripts/ringer/phase1/act2_guard_probe.py --arm $A --dry-run --out $OUT || { echo "WHY: dry run failed for arm $A"; exit 1; }
  $PY scripts/ringer/phase1/act2_guard_probe.py --check $OUT 12 --dry || { echo "WHY: dry check failed for arm $A"; exit 1; }
done
env -i PATH="$PATH" PYTHONPATH="$PYTHONPATH" $PY scripts/ringer/phase1/act2_guard_probe.py --arm control --out /tmp/g6-noconfirm-$$ >/dev/null 2>&1 && { echo "WHY: live mode without --confirm must refuse"; exit 1; }
F="scripts/ringer/phase1/act2_guard_probe.py tests/test_act2_guard_probe.py"
$PY -m ruff format --check $F && $PY -m ruff check $F || exit 1
if grep -n "requests\.\|urllib\|httpx" scripts/ringer/phase1/act2_guard_probe.py; then echo "WHY: direct network client in probe"; exit 1; fi
OUT=/home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/act2-visible-moves
mkdir -p $OUT && git add $F && git diff --cached > $OUT/guard-probe.patch && wc -l $OUT/guard-probe.patch && git diff --cached --stat | tail -4
